summary: All four features are implemented and build cleanly; three minor issues (double glass-card border, broad allergy substring match, consolidated endpoint swallowing auth errors) and one UX gap (silent reference-range parse failure) are flagged but none are blocking.
findings: Allergy cross-check false positives — checkAllergyHits uses String.includes on the raw allergy token; short tokens (e.g. 'ASA', 'in') can match unrelated drug name fragments. Use whole-word matching or enforce a minimum token length.

Consolidated endpoint error masking — the outer catch in DigitalTwin.jsx swallows all errors from GET /api/health-twin/ including 401/403/500 and falls through to the fallback silently. Auth errors should be re-thrown to surface an error state to the user.

Double glass-card border on Clinical Calculators — <details className='glass-card'> wraps the existing inner <div className='glass-card p-3 ...'>, nesting two elements with the glass-card border. The inner card's glass-card class should be removed.

Reference-range parser silent failure — isInRange returns null ('Unable to assess') for ranges with em dashes, Unicode operators, or appended units. When the range string is present but unparseable, the UI should display a brief note explaining why assessment is unavailable.
